title: Scout C2: daemon and bus entry points for dependency-driven gate/review/merge/dispatch
spec:
HARD OUTPUT CAP: JSON under 4,500 chars; ≤12 findings; evidence path:line only. Read-only. Skill trace-callers.
Trace: orchestrator/daemon.py tick() and main(); bus.create_task fields and update() restrictions (which fields the Planner owns; how a new `depends_on: list[str]` field would be stored and exposed via bus_mcp.bus_create_task); executor.start(task_id, prompt) and its fallback path; spawn.run_worker and spawn_review (mcp.py) for creating and running a review task; merge.merge(task_id, target) and merge.lock; how tests-green.sh is invoked (merge.py TESTS_GREEN, subprocess with cwd); how status/hold_reason are used. Then propose, with path:line anchors, the daemon state machine: for each queued execute task with all depends_on merged (task.merged_into set) and spec_review approved when complexity ≥5 → dispatch via executor.start(task_id, rendered prompt); for each done execute task without review → run gate on its worktree, create a review task (complexity ≥4; inputs [task]) and spawn it; for each review done with verdict approve → merge(task) into goal/<parent>; request_changes/failed/gate red → mark the execute task held with hold_reason and notify; idempotency guards needed (a `pipeline` field on the task json recording stage timestamps); which of these already exist. Note: the MCP server and the daemon are separate processes sharing pool_state.json and tasks/*.json — name the races.
acceptance: every entry point cited with path:line
state machine proposal with idempotency guards and the races between daemon and MCP server named

findings.claim: daemon.tick() only requeues running tasks whose pid died (>60s) and notifies on cooling/budget/codex-exhausted; no gate/review/merge/dispatch logic exists

bus.create_task locks spec/acceptance/scope/complexity Planner-only; update() raises PermissionError on those; depends_on isn't a field, and bus_mcp.bus_create_task omits constraints so it can't reach bus.create_task's constraints dict without a signature change
executor.start() picks an executor, claims the task, runs codex exec; _exhausted() falls back to spawn.run_worker on a Claude tier or holds with hold_reason
mcp.spawn_review/_bg spawn spawn.run_worker in a thread; run_worker builds review prompt from inputs[0]'s scoped diff, writes review_verdict onto review task and reviewed task
merge.merge() takes a global fcntl lock on merge.lock, rebases onto goal/<parent>, runs tests-green.sh with wt as argv[1], fast-forwards target only on green, sets merged_into+sha
no dedicated 'gate' script exists; tests-green.sh is the only gate, cd's into argv[1], exits 2 with failures-only stderr
status/hold_reason set via bus.update(status='held',hold_reason=...) at every stall: usage-limit, no-headroom, cooling executor, rebase conflict, tests_red
RACE: pool_state.json unlocked; daemon's long-lived Pool() and per-call fresh Pool() in the MCP process both read-modify-write via save(), losing cooldown/day_tokens/running updates under concurrency
RACE: bus.update() is get()+mutate+_save() with no lock; daemon requeue vs a worker's own bus.claim/post_result on the same task_id can interleave and drop one side's writes
nothing reads depends_on/merged_into to gate dispatch, runs the gate on done execute tasks to spawn a review, or auto-merges on approve/holds on reject: the daemon state machine is unimplemented

open_questions: depends_on: new bus.create_task param or reuse constraints{}?
daemon calls merge/spawn_review in-process or via MCP tools, to avoid a 2nd write path?
suggested_next: add pipeline{dispatched_at,gated_at,reviewed_at,merged_at}; daemon only advances a stage whose stamp is unset, inside the bus.update call
dispatch: execute+queued+all(depends_on merged)+(complexity<5 or review approved) -> executor.start once, guard dispatched_at

gate+review: execute+done+reviewed_at unset -> tests-green.sh on worktree; red->hold 'gate_red'; green->create review task(complexity>=4,inputs=[task])+spawn_review, stamp reviewed_at at dispatch to dedupe
merge: review+done+verdict=='approve' -> merge.merge(reviewed_task); else hold execute task hold_reason=verdict, notify()
add an flock around daemon-side bus.update/Pool.save before autonomous dispatch: today daemon only reads; this makes it write concurrently with MCP calls
